title: Verify Pyodide Blob conversion in the real browser before relying on Python mocks
applies_when: Python code running under Pyodide passes bytes, lists or option dictionaries into JavaScript Blob/XMLHttpRequest APIs. A native Python test can check call arguments but cannot establish the browser's proxy-conversion behavior.
lesson: Use a small real module-worker and loopback echo check before finalizing the fix. Pyodide can proxy Python bytes rather than turn them into a JavaScript byte buffer: a Blob built from an unconverted list containing bytes can send the Python repr, not the bytes. Explicitly convert Blob parts with pyodide.ffi.to_js and option dictionaries with dict_converter=Object.fromEntries; use a string 'type' key. Check received bytes and Content-Type, not merely Blob constructor arguments. Keep JSON serialization separate from interop: serialize the JSON value itself and distinguish omitted None from supported falsy values such as {}, [], False, 0 and ''. Retain no-body and conflicting-input controls, verify the imported production source, then add focused native mocks for the conversion protocol. Real browser checks and mock-based regression checks answer different questions.
avoid_when: This is not guidance to add Pyodide to ordinary CPython requests, or to require a browser for every Python bug. A mocked to_js identity function does not qualify actual JavaScript conversion. The observed runtime is Pyodide314.0.7/CPython3.14.2; other versions, binary payload families, cloud endpoints, browser policies and response paths need applicable checks. Worker XHR results do not establish main-thread synchronous-XHR support. Nine loopback cases and a native test-file pass do not prove full CI, universal correctness, speedup or a prospective evidence-selector advantage. Do not overwrite a valid caller's explicitly selected content-type policy merely because this particular shim had no such policy.

evidence.note: Official documentation distinguishes implicit conversion from proxying and documents explicit conversion. In particular, Python bytes are proxied to preserve round-trip type identity; a constructor accepting an object is not proof that it received the intended byte buffer. The stable documentation version can change.
The to_js API supports explicit conversion and a dict_converter. Choose the conversion expected by the actual JavaScript API instead of assuming a Python mapping is a JavaScript options object.

Published before/after real browser observations: object JSON originally sent null, five falsy JSON values sent no body, and b'hello' sent its repr with no MIME type. Candidate met nine loopback expectations, including two unchanged controls. Native Windows test_http_sync:65 pass; same focused tests on base:12 fail/8 pass. New native mocks explicitly check protocol only; upstream acceptance/CI and performance are not claimed.

Pinned submitted implementation serializes the supplied JSON, explicitly converts Blob parts/options, and keeps Pyodide imports local to the shim request method. This is a proposed repair, not evidence of a merged or portable result.
